On error it formats: if the context mark's line (0-based) != 0 use it, else if the problem mark's line != 0 use it; for SCANNER errors add 1 to that line (parser errors do not); if the resulting line != 0 the message is `yaml: line N: <problem>`, otherwise `yaml: <problem>`. The problem strings are libyaml's (e.g. \"found character that cannot start any token\", \"mapping values are not allowed in this context\", \"did not find expected key\", \"did not find expected ',' or ']'\", \"found unexpected end of stream\", \"could not find expected ':'\", \"did not find expected node content\", \"found a tab character that violates indentation\", \"block sequence entries are not allowed in this context\", \"found undefined tag handle\", \"did not find expected alphabetic or numeric character\", \"found unknown escape character\", etc.). Getting the marks right matters as much as the strings.\n\n## How to verify against the original\nThe original reads `.declscope.yaml` from the analyzed package's directory upward. Observed examples (input → message after the path):\n- `rules:\\n\\tfoo: 1\\n` → `yaml: line 2: found character that cannot start any token`\n- `: bad\\n` → `yaml: did not find expected key`\n- `key: value: other\\n` → `yaml: mapping values are not allowed in this context`\n- `rules:\\n  naming:\\n      qualify: always\\n    exported: true\\n` → `yaml: line 1: did not find expected key`\n- `filter:\\n  only: [a.go\\n` → `yaml: line 1: did not find expected ',' or ']'`\n- `filter:\\n  only: \"a.go\\n` → `yaml: line 2: found unexpected end of stream`\nValid documents produce no yaml error (other messages about unknown keys etc. may appear; those come from a different layer and are not your concern — but they tell you the document parsed). To check node values/positions of valid YAML you can rely on these config-layer messages: an unknown top-level key `foo` at line N prints `line N: unknown key \"foo\" (this section takes defaults, rules, filter, baseline)` (useful to verify Line numbers of mapping keys), and `rules:\\n  boundary: <value>` prints `rules.boundary: unknown mode \"<value>\" (want off or on)` with the decoded scalar value in Go %q form for any value other than off/on (useful to verify scalar decoding: quoting, escapes, folding, block scalars). `defaults:\\n  unexported: <value>` similarly prints `defaults.unexported: unknown scope \"<value>\" (want shared or private)`.\n\nTest broadly: at least ~150 inputs covering valid constructs and many kinds of malformed input (bad indentation at various depths and lines, unclosed quotes/flows at the first line vs later lines, tabs, stray `-` and `:`, bad escapes, duplicate anchors, undefined aliases (note: undefined alias errors may come from the decoder layer rather than the parser — record what you see), document markers, BOM, CRLF line endings, trailing spaces, empty file, comments only, `---` only). Aim for exact matches; when you cannot match something, note it.\n\nWrite clean, idiomatic Go with modest comments. Include a `yaml_test.go` with table tests of the error messages you verified. reports whether a potential simple key may still be one:\n// a key must end on its line and within 1024 characters.\nfunc (p *parser) simpleKeyIsValid(k *simpleKey) (valid, ok bool) {\n\tif !k.possible {\n\t\treturn false, true\n\t}\n\tif k.mark.line < p.mark.line || k.mark.index+1024 < p.mark.index {\n\t\tif k.required {\n\t\t\treturn false, p.setScannerError(\"while scanning a simple key\", k.mark,\n\t\t\t\t\"could not find expected ':'\")\n\t\t}\n\t\tk.possible = false\n\t\treturn false, true\n\t}\n\treturn true, true\n}\n\n// saveSimpleKey records that a simple key may start at the current position.\nfunc (p *parser) saveSimpleKey() bool {\n\t// A simple key is required where a block collection expects its next\n\t// key: in the block context, at the indentation column.\n\trequired := p.flowLevel == 0 && p.indent == p.mark.column\n\tif p.simpleKeyAllowed {\n\t\tk := simpleKey{\n\t\t\tpossible:    true,\n\t\t\trequired:    required,\n\t\t\ttokenNumber: p.tokensParsed + len(p.tokens) - p.tokensHead,\n\t\t\tmark:        p.mark,\n\t\t}\n\t\tif !p.removeSimpleKey() {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t\tp.simpleKeys[len(p.simpleKeys)-1] = k\n\t\tp.simpleKeysByTok[k.tokenNumber] = len(p.simpleKeys) - 1\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// removeSimpleKey drops the potential simple key of the current flow level,\n// failing if it was required.\nfunc (p *parser) removeSimpleKey() bool {\n\ti := len(p.simpleKeys) - 1\n\tif p.simpleKeys[i].possible {\n\t\tif p.simpleKeys[i].required {\n\t\t\treturn p.setScannerError(\"while scanning a simple key\", p.simpleKeys[i].mark,\n\t\t\t\t\"could not find expected ':'\")\n\t\t}\n\t\tp.simpleKeys[i].possible = false\n\t\tdelete(p.simpleKeysByTok, p.simpleKeys[i].tokenNumber)\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) increaseFlowLevel() bool {\n\tp.simpleKeys = append(p.simpleKeys, simpleKey{mark: p.mark})\n\tp.flowLevel++\n\tif p.flowLevel > maxFlowLevel {\n\t\treturn p.setScannerError(\"while increasing flow level\", p.simpleKeys[len(p.simpleKeys)-1].mark,\n\t\t\tfmt.Sprintf(\"exceeded max depth of %d\", maxFlowLevel))\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) p.simpleKeys[:last]\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// Indentation.\n\n// rollIndent opens a block collection when column is deeper than the current\n// indentation, queueing its start token at position number (an absolute\n// token number), or at the end if number is -1.\nfunc (p *parser) rollIndent(column, number int, typ tokenType, m mark) bool {\n\tif p.flowLevel > 0 {\n\t\treturn true\n\t}\n\tif p.simpleKeys[len(p.simpleKeys)-1].mark,\n\t\t\t\tfmt.Sprintf(\"exceeded max depth of %d\", maxIndents))\n\t\t}\n\t\tif number > -1 {\n\t\t\tnumber -= p.tokensParsed\n\t\t}\n\t\tp.insertToken(number, token{typ: typ, start: m, end: m})\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// unrollIndent closes the block collections deeper than column.\nfunc (p *parser) unrollIndent(column int) bool {\n\tif p.flowLevel > 0 p.indents[:len(p.indents)-1]\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// Fetching tokens.\n\nfunc (p *parser) fetchStreamStart() bool {\n\tp.indent = -1\n\tp.simpleKeys = append(p.simpleKeys, simpleKey{})\n\tp.simpleKeysByTok = make(map[int]int)\n\tp.simpleKeyAllowed = true\n\tp.streamStartProduced = true\n\tp.insertToken(-1, token{typ: tokStreamStart, start: p.mark, end: p.mark})\n\treturn true\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) fetchStreamEnd() bool {\n\t// Force a new line.\n\tif p.mark.column != 0 {\n\t\tp.mark.column = 0\n\t\tp.mark.line++\n\t}\n\tif !p.unrollIndent(-1) || fetchDirective() bool {\n\tif !p.unrollIndent(-1) || !p.removeSimpleKey() {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tp.simpleKeyAllowed = false\n\tvar t token\n\tif !p.scanDirective(&t) {\n\t\treturn p.mark})\n\treturn true\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) fetchFlowEntry() bool {\n\tif !p.removeSimpleKey() {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tp.simpleKeyAllowed = true\n\tstart := p.mark\n\tp.skip()\n\tp.insertToken(-1, token{typ: tokFlowEntry, start: start, end: p.mark})\n\treturn true\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) fetchBlockEntry() bool {\n\tif p.flowLevel == 0 {\n\t\tif !p.simpleKeyAllowed {\n\t\t\treturn p.setScannerError(\"\", p.mark, \"block sequence entries are not allowed in this context\")\n\t\t}\n\t\tif !p.rollIndent(p.mark.column, -1, tokBlockSequenceStart, !p.simpleKeyAllowed {\n\t\t\treturn p.setScannerError(\"\", p.mark, \"mapping keys are not allowed in this context\")\n\t\t}\n\t\tif !p.rollIndent(p.mark.column, -1, tokBlockMappingStart, p.mark) start: start, end: p.mark})\n\treturn true\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) fetchValue() bool {\n\tk := &p.simpleKeys[len(p.simpleKeys)-1]\n\tvalid, ok := p.simpleKeyIsValid(k)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn false\n\t\tdelete(p.simpleKeysByTok, k.tokenNumber)\n\t\t// A simple key cannot follow another simple key.\n\t\tp.simpleKeyAllowed = false\n\t} else {\n\t\t// The ':' follows a complex key, or no key at all.\n\t\tif p.flowLevel == 0 {\n\t\t\tif !p.simpleKeyAllowed {\n\t\t\t\treturn p.setScannerError(\"\", p.mark, \"mapping values are not allowed in this context\")\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif simple key.\n\tif !p.saveSimpleKey() {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tp.simpleKeyAllowed = false\n\tvar t token\n\tif !p.scanAnchor(&t, typ) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tp.insertToken(-1, t)\n\treturn {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tp.insertToken(-1, t)\n\treturn true\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) fetchBlockScalar(literal bool) bool {\n\tif !p.removeSimpleKey() {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\t// A simple key may !p.scanPlainScalar(&t) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tp.insertToken(-1, t)\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// Whitespace and comments.\n\n// scanToNextToken skips whitespace, comments and line breaks.\nfunc (p *parser) scanToNextToken() bool {\n\tfor {\n\t\t// A byte order mark is allowed at the start of a line.\n\t\tif p.unread < 1 && !p.updateBuffer(1) {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t\tif p.mark.column == 0 && p.isBOM(0) {\n\t\t\tp.skip()\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t// Tabs are allowed in the flow context, and in the block context\n\t\t// where no simple key may start: not at the start of a line nor\n\t\t// after Like yaml.v3,\n// which collects head and foot comments here, it goes on through following\n// lines that hold only blanks and comments, up to the end of the last\n// comment, without the tab restrictions of scanToNextToken.\nfunc (p *parser) scanComments() bool {\n\tfor peek := 0; peek < 512; peek++ {\n\t\tif p.unread < peek+1 && !p.updateBuffer(peek+1) {\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t\tif p.isBlank(peek) {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tc := p.at(peek)\n\t\tif p.flowLevel > 0 && (c == ']' || c == '}') {\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t\tif p.isBreakz(peek) {\n\t\t\tif !p.isBreak(peek) {\n\t\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif c != '#' {\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t\tseen := p.mark.index + peek\n\t\tfor {\n\t\t\tif p.unread < 1 && !p.updateBuffer(1) {\n\t\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif p.isBreakz(0) {\n\t\t\t\tif p.mark.index >= seen {\n\t\t\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tif p.unread < 2 && !p.updateBuffer(2) {\n\t\t\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tp.skipLine()\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tp.skip()\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\t// The next round starts past the line break that ends the comment.\n\t\tpeek = 0\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// scanLineComment consumes a comment that follows a token on its line, as\n// yaml.v3 does to keep it as the token's line comment. It skips tabs too.\nfunc (p *parser) scanLineComment() bool {\n\tif p.newlines > 0 {\n\t\treturn true\n\t}\n\tfor peek := 0; peek < 512; peek++ {\n\t\tif p.unread < peek+1 && !p.updateBuffer(peek+1) {\n\t\t\t\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\tp.skipLine()\n\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\tp.skip()\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tbreak\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// Directives.\n\nfunc (p *parser) scanDirective(t *token) bool {\n\tstart := p.mark\n\tp.skip() // '%'\n\n\tvar name []byte\n\tif !p.scanDirectiveName(start, &name) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tswitch string(name) {\n\tcase of the line, including any comment.\n\tif p.unread < 1 && !p.updateBuffer(1) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tfor p.isBlank(0) {\n\t\tp.skip()\n\t\tif p.unread < 1 && !p.updateBuffer(1) {\n\t\t\treturn {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t\tp.skipLine()\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) scanDirectiveName(start mark, name *[]byte) bool {\n\tif p.unread < 1 && !p.updateBuffer(1) {\n\t\treturn \"found unexpected non-alphabetical character\")\n\t}\n\t*name = s\n\treturn true\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) scanVersionDirectiveValue(start mark, major, minor *int8) bool {\n\tif p.unread < 1 && p.unread < 1 && !p.updateBuffer(1) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tvar value, length int8\n\tfor isDigit(p.at(0)) {\n\t\tlength++\n\t\tif length > maxNumberLength {\n\t\t\treturn p.setScannerError(\"while true\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) scanTagDirectiveValue(start mark, handle, prefix *[]byte) bool {\n\tif p.unread < 1 && !p.updateBuffer(1) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tfor p.isBlank(0) {\n\t\tp.skip()\n\t\tif p.unread < 1 && !p.updateBuffer(1) {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tvar handleValue, prefixValue []byte\n\tif !p.scanTagHandle(true, start, &handleValue) {\n\t\treturn {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tif p.unread < 1 && !p.updateBuffer(1) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tif !p.isBlankz(0) {\n\t\treturn p.setScannerError(\"while scanning a %TAG directive\", start, \"did not find expected whitespace or line break\")\n\t}\n\t*handle = handleValue\n\t*prefix = prefixValue\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// Anchors, aliases and tags.\n\nfunc (p *parser) scanAnchor(t *token, typ tokenType) bool {\n\tstart := p.mark\n\tp.skip() // '&' or '*'\n\n\tif p.unread < 1 && !p.updateBuffer(1) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tvar s []byte\n\tfor isAlpha(p.at(0)) {\n\t\ts = p.read(s)\n\t\tif p.unread < 1 && !p.updateBuffer(1) {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tend := p.mark\n\n\t// The name must be followed by a blank or one of the indicators\n\t// '?', ':', ',', ']', '}', '%', '@' and '`'.\n\tif len(s) == 0 || !(p.isBlankz(0) || strings.IndexByte(\"?:,]}%@`\", p.at(0)) >= 0) {\n\t\tcontext := \"while scanning an alias\"\n\t\tif typ == tokAnchor {\n\t\t\tcontext = \"while scanning true\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) scanTag(t *token) bool {\n\tstart := p.mark\n\tvar handle, suffix []byte\n\n\tif p.unread < 2 && !p.updateBuffer(2) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tif p.at(1) == '<' {\n\t\t// A verbatim tag, !<...>: the handle stays empty.\n\t\tp.skip()\n\t\tp.skip()\n\t\tif !p.scanTagURI(true, false, nil, start, &suffix) {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t\tif p.at(0) != '>' {\n\t\t\treturn On error it formats: if the context mark's line (0-based) != 0 use it, else if the problem mark's line != 0 use it; for SCANNER errors add 1 to that line (parser errors do not); if the resulting line != 0 the message is `yaml: line N: <problem>`, otherwise `yaml: <problem>`. It is written inside its type, so its namespace is the type's file's, and the type's directive reaches it.\n\nA **method with a receiver** is not a member.
